title: Commutativity of the full probabilistic powerdomain monad
formal: Editorial subprobability variant: for all dcpos X,Y, all continuous subprobability valuations mu on X and nu on Y, and every Scott-continuous \(f:X\times Y\to[0,\infty]\), must \[\int_X\!\left(\int_Y f(x,y)\,d\nu(y)\right)d\mu(x)=\int_Y\!\left(\int_X f(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\right)d\nu(y)\,?\] This is commutativity of the full continuous-subprobability valuation monad.
definitions:
A dcpo is a partially ordered set in which each nonempty directed subset has a supremum. A directed set is one in which every finite subset has an upper bound within the set. A Scott-open subset is upward closed and, whenever a directed supremum belongs to it, contains an element of that directed set. A map is Scott-continuous when it is monotone and preserves directed suprema. X×Y has the componentwise dcpo order and its Scott topology; do not substitute a potentially different topological product of Scott spaces. The target [0,infinity] has its usual order and Scott topology.

A continuous subprobability valuation mu assigns a number in [0,1] to each Scott-open U, with mu(empty)=0, mu(X)≤1, monotonicity, modularity mu(U)+mu(V)=mu(U union V)+mu(U intersection V), and preservation of suprema of directed families of open sets. For a nonnegative Scott-continuous h define its integral by the layer-cake formula integral_0^infinity mu({x:h(x)>t}) dt, allowing infinity. Iterated integrals in the statement use this definition.

The monad orders valuations pointwise; its unit sends x to the Dirac valuation U↦1 if x∈U, zero otherwise. For a Scott-continuous kernel K:X→V(Y), extension maps mu to U↦integral_X K(x)(U)dmu(x). These definitions specify the same independence-interchange question through the displayed Fubini identity. All continuous valuations of total mass at most one are allowed, not just finite combinations of Dirac valuations or their directed-supremum closure, called minimal valuations. Choosing total mass at most one is an explicit specialization; the card does not claim equivalence with every unbounded-mass convention.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the displayed identity for the entire stated domain, or explicit dcpos, continuous subprobability valuations and a Scott-continuous integrand with different iterated integrals. A nonminimal valuation alone is not a counterexample, and commutativity proved only for minimal valuations does not settle the full class.
context:
Goubault-Larrecq’s 2024 discussion separates the unresolved commutativity of the classical full valuation construction from commutative replacements such as minimal valuations.

Goubault-Larrecq and Jia construct continuous valuations outside smaller valuation classes. Their separation does not itself prove failure of a Fubini equation.
why: Commutativity determines whether a central denotational model supports unrestricted exchange of probabilistic effects.

import_provenance.original_title: Commutativity of the full probabilistic powerdomain monad
import_provenance.original_statement: Is the monad of all continuous valuations on dcpos commutative: can the order of two independent probabilistic computations always be exchanged? Goubault-Larrecq’s semantics obtains this property for minimal valuations, but the full continuous-valuation monad remains the open target.

sentences: Continuous valuations generalize probability distributions on ordered semantic domains.
The question asks whether the order of two integrations can always be exchanged.
The selected variant uses subprobability mass and the Scott topology of the dcpo product.
Minimal valuations form a smaller class for which separate positive results are available.
Separation from that class does not by itself refute the interchange equation.
